title: The Face Taking Shape
logline: A sculptor has spent three weeks on the eyes of a Buddha image and still isn't satisfied. He won't say what he's looking for, only that he'll know it when the face stops looking back.
human_question: What is someone actually doing when they hold one thing in mind, in detail, for weeks?

premise.story: The final stage of carving or casting a Buddha image, following the maker's attention to the face specifically.
premise.place: A family image-making workshop: tools, half-finished figures, plaster dust or clay.
premise.experience: The strange patience of working on a face that isn't looking back yet, and the moment it starts to.

concept_links.why: One method of recollecting the Buddha is careful, head-to-feet attention to an image until it can be held in the mind [C091-M:L7].
Workability and proficiency describe a craft made usable through long, repeated attention, exactly the labour visible in this workshop [C023-P:L149; C023-P:L153-L157].

what_camera_could_observe: Tools, dust and half-finished figures in the workshop
Long, silent attention to one feature at a time
Checking proportions against reference or memory
The moment the eyes, specifically, are finished
what_must_be_real: The maker's actual working method and his own account of it. The film must not frame him as practising a meditation he may not himself do; his own words must lead.

possible_arc.turn: The slow, repeated work on the eyes over days.
possible_arc.ending_open: The finished face, and whatever the maker actually says about it, or doesn't.

requirements: A family or workshop currently completing a Buddha image, willing to allow filming over enough time
Access to the maker's own account of his process and beliefs, not assumptions imposed on him
No disruption to a live commission

suggestions.name: A family Buddha-image workshop
suggestions.why: Region-level suggestion; traditional image-making workshops exist in and around these areas.
suggestions.verify: No specific workshop or maker has been identified or confirmed.

risks: Implying the craftsman practises this specific meditation without his confirmation
Commercial pressures on the family's work being edited out to keep a purely pious picture
drop_if: No workshop will allow the camera into the actual working process over enough time to show real patience, not a summary

connections.note: Sustained, patient attention to one held-in-mind good thing here leads into sustained, patient care for people in the later, harder film.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
